status: User-requested exploratory extension, specified before polarization fits after earlier historical results were inspected
scope: Verified annual ProQuest claims 1900–2010 only; all existing source exports, model files and reports preserved

features.political_polarization: Mean absolute Democratic–Republican yes-share difference across House rollcalls, using only actual yea/nay codes 1/6, at least five actual voters in each party per rollcall, and at least ten eligible rollcalls in twelve complete months t-13 through t-2. The immediately preceding month is a reporting buffer. Range 0–1. Independents and ambiguous member-party mappings are excluded. This measures realized legislative partisan separation, not the standard NOMINATE ideological gap or mass affective polarization.
features.forecast_polarization: Mean 4*p_positive*p_negative in general-business forecasts over t-3 through t-1, using existing equal-article-within-paper and equal-paper monthly shares. Range 0–1; maximal for equally sized opposing camps, zero if either camp is absent. Same support gate as existing disagreement_3m: two months, two papers, five articles. Not political newspaper slant. Existing three-class Gini disagreement and paper dispersion remain where already present.

learned_models: original vintage macro logistic core and CPI
original vintage macro plus press logistic core and CPI
selected vintage macro logistic core and CPI
selected vintage macro plus press logistic core and CPI
controls: Constant prevalence and historical/recent class-frequency forecasts remain feature-free controls. Adding regressors would change their definition.
comparability: Preserve each existing model's splits, target, training rows, regularization, article/month weights and evaluation origins. For selected macro models reuse the training-only selections already saved; do not retune using polarization outcomes. Baseline refits must reproduce saved logistic predictions within tolerance before comparisons are accepted. GRU baseline is rerun with identical seeds under the same environment as augmented models.
preprocessing: Each added scalar has a training-only median imputation (zero fallback), training-only standardization, and missingness indicator. Do not drop rows for new-feature missingness. RNN and its two logistic controls receive the same monthly scalar inputs in their claim/head input; existing preceding-12-month sequence remains identical. No new interactions or hyperparameter search.

rnn.epoch_selection: validation log loss only, existing early stopping

evaluation: Primary incremental effect: baseline loss minus augmented loss, paired on identical rows, reported for each arm and model. Binary Brier for claim correctness and multiclass summed Brier for monthly direction are separate estimands. Report log loss, accuracy, class discrimination, calibration, and 2007–2009 exclusion. Five-year-block intervals condition on fitted predictions; no causal effect claim or fresh holdout claim.
limitations: Current NOMINATE career estimates are not print-time predictors and are excluded. Dated historical rollcalls are reconstructed from today's database, not archival release vintages. Agenda, participation and party structure affect the political proxy. Forecast polarity reflects the selected query and changing paper coverage, not the entire press. Both vary at a monthly level, not independently across claims. Modern claims remain excluded.
